vo_duration_s.description: Measured voiceover duration — the master clock.

sections.description: The six-section spine with resolved start times.

layout.description: Grid/Flex strategy in one line, e.g. 'grid 60/40, plate left, type right'

plate.description: Project-relative path to the plate, or null for browser-drawn. Never an absolute or file:// path.

intent.description: A visual state, not a sentence.

easing.description: Mapped to a GSAP ease by the generator. Kept for compatibility; when present it OVERRIDES the idiom's own ease. Never one easing for everything — and the generator no longer emits a timeline `defaults:{ease}`, so an unnamed ease is GSAP's default, not the piece's [S6/A-10].

idiom.description: Motion idiom by narrative function [S6/A-10, R8]. `arrive` = the fade-and-rise (opacity+y, power3.out) — now ONE option among six, not the house entrance. `slam` = kinetic-beat-slam (opacity+scale 1.12→1, power4.out), a percussive spoken hit. `wipe` = a clip-path reveal, opacity untouched, power2.inOut — geometric, so it carries a `staysInFrame` assertion rather than `appearsBy`. `count` = counting-dynamic-scale: `text` must contain a number, rendered as a tabular-nums counter driven by a proxy `onUpdate` plus scale 0.86→1, power2.out; forces the `stat` type role. `swap` = scale-swap-transition: this beat and the one before it share a grid slot, previous shrinks away (power2.in) while this pops in (back.out(1.6)) — transform, don't replace. `hold` = multi-phase-camera micro-drift on the stage for the beat's own `dur`; emits NO element, which is how a deliberate long-form hold is sanctioned by cadence instead of padded. A majority of real tweens sharing one idiom+ease signature is the template failure regardless of content.

actor.description: Shared id for the same on-screen actor across beats and scenes [S6/A-9]. An actor appearing in two CONSECUTIVE scenes as separate beats is warned: either merge those scenes into one hand-authored multi-phase sub-composition (`handoff: "hand-authored"`, hyperframes-core composition-patterns §C "Multi-scene merge") so the actor is REARRANGED rather than redrawn, or accept that the diagram is being rebuilt.

text.description: The on-screen type for this beat. Falls back to `caption`, then `intent`.

role.description: Type role; drives the class and therefore the type floor.

bg.description: This scene's ground. A plain `crossfade` across a ground change is rejected at generation; `push-slide` / `zoom-through` / `squeeze` never blend grounds; `blur-crossfade` blends under blur — extract its midpoint [S7/R-2]. Shorts default to `cut`.

transition.description: The ENTERING transition for this scene (registry convention: a scene names the transition that brings it ON). Omit to accept the derived default: `short` format → `cut`; `long` → `push-slide LEFT` inside a section and `zoom-through` 0.4s at a section start. The first scene's transition must be absent or `cut`. Authored time still TILES — scenes have no gap and no overlap in the beat sheet; the generator DERIVES the overlap window (outgoing `data-duration` extended by d, incoming `data-start` pulled earlier by d, track ping-pong, the registry `gsap_template` stamped on `window.__timelines['main']` at T = overlap start). Never author the overlap yourself. More than 3 distinct non-cut types in one video is warned — pick 2-3 and repeat them. Exit animations are never emitted: the transition IS the exit. [S6/A-8, TRANSITION-REGISTRY.md]

type.description: A registry name, or `cut`. `crossfade` where this scene's resolved `bg` differs from the previous scene's is a GENERATION ERROR — the midpoint is a muddy blend of two grounds; use `blur-crossfade` (the blur masks the clash) or a `push-slide` (no frame blends two grounds).

direction.description: `push-slide` only, and the only place a direction is meaningful — "vertical push" is a direction, not a transition name. Default LEFT. One direction per section.

duration.description: Overlap length in seconds. Registry cap 2.0s; typical 0.3-0.6s. Omit for the registry default (crossfade 0.5, blur-crossfade 0.6, push-slide 0.5, zoom-through 0.4, squeeze 0.4).

handoff.description: `hand-authored` means this scene's sub-composition file is written by hand (a multi-scene merge with persistent actors, a camera leg, anything the six idioms cannot express) and the generator MUST NOT overwrite it [S6/A-9]. The generator still owns the clip, the derived transition, and the assertions, so a hand-authored file must honour the id contract: `#<scene-id>-b<N>` per beat and `#<scene-id>-stage` for the stage, or `check` reports `motion_selector_missing`.

bg.description: Default canvas background (hex). Per-scene `bg` overrides it.

accent.description: Default accent (hex). Exactly one accent per frame [S6/A-2].

fonts.description: A named Google Fonts family is the engine-supported path: the compiler injects deterministic @font-face at render time.

css.description: The CSS font-family stack, including fallbacks.

safe_area.description: Safe-area insets in px. Declared here and CONSUMED as .stage padding by the generator.

audio.description: Optional bed mounted on the root. Plain data-volume only — a data-automation lane REPLACES it on this engine.

muted.description: Muted ink for disclosure flags. Never the accent — a flag in the accent colour reads as a citation.
